title: Canary rollout + PRD edits — daily scratchpad
content:
Morning dump — pulling together things I want to resolve before EOD. Low-polish, just a brain-dump so I don't forget follow-ups.

Context:
- Canary rollout for token-prefix caching (v1) targeting hosted-api models. Objective: reduce avg token latency by ~8-15% for short-chat flows while keeping p95 under SLA.
- PRD edits in progress: behavioral expectations section, fallback policy details, observability hooks.
- Key stakeholders: Jordan (SRE/observability), Maya (Security/Compliance), Carlos (Sales/Customer ops).

Open questions / decisions to make:
- Fallback policy: automatic downgrade to smaller-quantized variant OR route to secondary region? Pros/cons: region fallback increases latency spike for some users; model downgrade changes semantics (might cause hallucination). Need Jordan's input on p95 transient behavior.
- Telemetry naming: are we comfortable using metric name "cache.prefix_hit_ratio" or should it be "cache.kv_prefix_hit" to match infra conventions? Ask Jordan.
- Legal: does adding KV-prefetch count as processing customer tokens for purposes of retention policy? Maya to confirm.

TODOS (short term - today / tomorrow):
- [ ] Sync with Jordan (SRE) — ask for synthetic canary harness run & p50/p95 expectations by EOD. Slack ping: @jordan — note: ask for trace-level sample for tokenization step.
- [ ] Update PRD section 4.1 fallback flows — draft text that lists 3 fallback tiers (region, model-variant, degraded-output) and call out user-visible errors.
- [ ] Add rollout guard rails to PRD: "max concurrent canary = 5% traffic", "auto-rollback threshold: 3% error increase OR p95 > 1.8x baseline for 10m". Confirm thresholds with SRE.
- [ ] Quick one-pager for Sales (Carlos): short bullet list of customer-facing messaging if we expose "faster responses via cache" as a product benefit (risks: consistency). Deliver draft by tomorrow morning.
- [ ] Ask Maya about KMS access for cache keys — do we need extra attestation for private deployments?
- [ ] Create Jira tasks for infra: PROJ-2145 is current epic, need child tickets: cache-instrumentation, canary-routing, rollback automation. Add acceptance criteria.

PRD edit notes (copy-paste fragments to integrate):
- Section: Observability hooks (new)
  - "Expose per-request tag 'cache_hit' with values: miss/prefetch/hit-remote/hit-local. Sample traces at 1% by default, 10% for canary window. Include token-latency histogram by sequence length bucket (0-32, 33-128, 129+)."
- Section: Failure modes
  - "Cache poisoning: if outputs depended on cache incorrectly, allow immediate rollback and invalidate cache. Add metric 'cache.invalidation.events' and an alert if > 5/min during rollout."
- Section: Customer impact & messaging
  - "Default behavior: no user-visible config. Beta customers can opt into 'aggressive caching' that may change cost profile. Sales must communicate possible micro-delta in completions."

Meeting notes from 2026-03-12 sync (short):
- Jordan: wants longer warm-up (10k requests) for synthetic canary to stabilize kernel scheduling jitter. Also suggested sampling at different seq lengths.
- Maya: initial read — prefers explicit note that cache keys do NOT include any PII and that we store only token ids + model-version. Wants a short privacy rationale paragraph in PRD.
- Carlos: asked for a simple fallback script for CS to run if a customer complains; suggested adding a "customer visible status" field so we can tell them if their traffic was in canary.

Risks / mitigations:
- Risk: Can cause output drift for prompt-sensitive flows. Mitigation: limited canary, prompt-level unit tests, eval set to run nightly with canary enabled and compare ROUGE/BLEU/LM-consistency metrics.
- Risk: Increased tail latency during cache warm-up. Mitigation: staged warm-up with controlled traffic bursts; pre-warm via synthetic replay.

Quick eval checklist (to add to PRD):
- [ ] Baseline eval set (100 prompts) run vs canary and baseline.
- [ ] Automated diff & per-prompt flagging (>= 10% token-output difference) -> manual review.
- [ ] Per-customer opt-in metrics — show cache effectiveness by customer id (anonymized).

Notes to self (random):
- Remember to update the Console rollout UI copy: "Canary: up to X% of traffic; rollouts can auto-fallback on anomalies."
- Check older Confluence draft dated 2025-11-02 — there was a paragraph about 'prefix hashing' that might be reusable.
- If we expose any of this as a product feature, Ops needs a toggle per-tenant. File a ticket for tenant toggle.

Communication plan sketch:
- Week 0 (internal): SRE + Security + CS review
- Week 1 (small canary): 5% traffic, 72h observe, daily health checks
- Week 2 (ramp): 20% traffic, 48h blocks, run evals overnight
- Week 3: wide rollout if no regressions

End-of-day checklist (for me):
- [ ] Jordan sync (blocked on synthetic run)
- [ ] PRD draft updated with Observability & Failure Modes sections
- [ ] Draft one-pager for Carlos
- [ ] Split tickets under PROJ-2145 and assign owners

Random TODO to file later: create a small demo script (python) that shows difference in latency with/without cache for short conversation. Put in repo: infra/example-cache-demo.

If I don't come back to this doc, at least I wrote the things down.

-- Bina
